title: Blanche of Castile Raises a King
text:
When King Louis VIII of France died in November 1226, his son and heir, Louis IX, was only twelve. His mother, Blanche of Castile, a granddaughter of Eleanor of Aquitaine, took charge as regent. Powerful barons, thinking a foreign-born woman and a child easy prey, rose in revolt. Blanche outmaneuvered them with armies and diplomacy and held the kingdom together until her son came of age.

She raised Louis herself, with great strictness and piety. His friend and biographer Jean de Joinville, who knew him well, records what she used to say to him: that she loved him more than any mortal, but that she would rather see him dead than know he had committed a mortal sin. Louis remembered these words all his life, and became famous for his justice and devotion. After his death he was canonized as Saint Louis.

Blanche's love was also possessive. Joinville tells that she was so jealous of Louis's young wife, Margaret of Provence, that the couple had to meet secretly on a staircase in the castle at Pontoise between their two rooms, with servants posted to warn them when the queen mother was coming.

When Louis left on crusade in 1248, he again left the kingdom in his mother's hands. She governed until her death in 1252. Louis heard the news in the Holy Land, and Joinville says he mourned her deeply.
lesson: Firm principles given in childhood can shape a whole life. But even a devoted parent must learn to let a grown child have a life of his own.
people: Blanche of Castile, Louis IX (Saint Louis), Margaret of Provence, Jean de Joinville
source: Jean de Joinville, Life of Saint Louis
